page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 12 dedicated physical cores, each running a single thread, resulting in 12 vCPUs. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only large block transfers reaching 59.2 GB/sec and write operations at 49.35 GB/sec, though the overall Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, processing 8.48 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.3xlarge offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which aligns with its 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This instance is best suited for workloads such as in-memory caching, database operations, moderate multi-threaded data processing, and general-purpose applications requiring a larger memory footprint without intensive single-core compute demands.
